Today's macOS Tahoe 26.7 candidate release includes a short video that appears to demonstrate the Visual Intelligence feature of Apple's rumored camera-equipped AirPods. You can see it below.

macOS 26.7 contains a demo video of camera-equipped AirPods

MacRumors discovered a short video in today's macOS Tahoe 26.7 RC, in which a man wearing AirPods appears to ask Siri to note down the book he is reading. Siri's voiceover says:

The camera itself cannot be seen in the video, and the earphones look very similar to the current AirPods Pro. The most obvious difference is that the stem section appears slightly thicker.

Aaron Perris has also posted the same video on X:

Bloomberg's Mark Gurman previously reported that Apple may launch camera-equipped AirPods as early as this year, with the internal codename B790. Earlier today, MacRumors also found references to B790 in macOS 26.7 RC, including code for "image stream".

It is worth noting that these AirPods are reportedly separate from another camera-equipped model that Bloomberg has said Apple has been developing, internally codenamed B798, which is not expected to launch until 2027.

Given Apple's decision to bury this demo video within macOS 26.7 RC, these camera-equipped AirPods have a high chance of being officially unveiled at next month's iPhone event.

What do you think of this video? Let us know in the comments.
